new_results.statement: For Y=hX^2+X S(V)+R(V), with X an original independent cap-one coordinate, arbitrary h and arbitrary correlation between S and R, a bank submeasure of mass m and unnormalized slope density cap L obeys nu_Y{|Y-t|<rho} <= m sqrt(G(4(L/m)rho)), G(q)=2q(1+log(1/(2q))) for q<=1/2 and 1 above. After an outer indefinite pair (D,kappa), ||p_Q^sub||inf <=8sqrt(mL/kappa)+C_*m/sqrt(D), C_*=4.004506265397... .

For any positive finite/countable bank decomposition with masses m_j and unnormalized slope caps L_j<=H0 m_j, summing the arbitrary-self compiler preserves exactly 8sqrt(H0/kappa)+C_*/sqrt(D), with no fragment-count, location, diameter, support, moment or translation tax.

For an actual block [[C,b,F],[b^T,d,g^T],[F^T,g,E]] with C an invertible indefinite original-coordinate pair, h=d-b^TC^-1b and a=g-F^TC^-1b, exact completion leaves hX_i^2+X_i[beta+2a^TV]+R(V). If a!=0, Claude Lemma 1 implies ||p_Q||inf<=8/sqrt(kappa||a||_2)+C_*/sqrt(D); the sharper product-projection cap improves 8 to 8/2^(1/4). The estimate is uniform in arbitrary h.

Combining the arbitrary-self compiler with account03/B14 r32, a remainder hX0^2+X0[s0+2d(aX3+bX4-beta)]+R with |b|>=|a| retains ||p_Q||inf<=4sqrt(2)/sqrt(|db|kappa)+C_*/sqrt(D) under arbitrary finite/countable positive fragmentation of X3 while X4 remains whole, for every h.

For Q_{epsilon,m}=epsilon^-1 U1^2-epsilon U2^2+epsilon X^2+2epsilon^-1 X w_m^T V, epsilon<=1/2, the exact target holds and the whole-bank bound is <=8+C_* uniformly in epsilon,m, while conditioning all bank coordinates but one and applying the same compiler gives only 4sqrt(2)m^(1/4)+C_*. This is not a density lower bound or QFORM counterexample.

first_unpaid_implication: QFORM-SCHUR-LEAKAGE-OR-WHOLE-VOLUME-EXIT-v1: before active-law fragmentation in every surviving no-pivot/N3 state, expose either an original-coordinate invertible indefinite pair with quantitatively useful whole-bank Schur-direction leakage a, now paid for arbitrary residual self curvature; or a whole-law D'/D5/ridge/mixed-hub/bank exit; or a new outside-curvature mechanism.
